<objective>
Harden the tracer's minimal supervision into the full RUN-03…RUN-06 contract: a wall-clock cap that
leaves no orphans, stdout parsing that cannot crash the daemon and never drives a state transition,
session resume, and the runtime `apiKeySource` assertion that is the independent second layer of the
billing guarantee.

Purpose: the tracer proves the happy path completes. This plan proves the unhappy paths terminate
cleanly — the session that hangs, the line that will not parse, the event type nobody has documented,
and the credential that got in by a route the env allowlist could not reach.

Output: a `WorktreeRunner` that survives every malformed input the fixture can produce and reaps its
whole process group, plus `rate-limit.ts` and `evidence-trap.ts` promoted out of `src/spikes/` into
production with their tests in the default `npm test` run.
</objective>

  <behavior>
    - Spawning the `hang` fixture with a 500 ms wall-clock cap results in the child being dead within 2 seconds, a `TIMEOUT` event recorded, and the task in `failed`.
    - The grandchild pid the `hang` fixture reports is also dead: `process.kill(grandchildPid, 0)` throws with `code === 'ESRCH'`.
    - Spawning the `happy-path` fixture with a 30-second cap records no `TIMEOUT` event, and no timer remains scheduled after the run (asserted by the process exiting cleanly under the test runner without an open-handle warning).
    - `killTree()` called against a pid that has already exited returns normally rather than throwing.
    - `killTree()` on a child that ignores `SIGTERM` still terminates it after the grace window via `SIGKILL`.
    - The resolved wall-clock cap is `String`-free: it is a number of milliseconds, resolved task > `.fleet.yml` > Fleet config > 1_800_000, and a non-positive or non-integer configured value is rejected rather than silently coerced.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Harden `killTree(pid, graceMs)` in `src/runner/worktree-runner.ts` to the exact shape RESEARCH.md
verified: `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')` against the whole process group, then a
`setTimeout(() =&gt; { try { process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch { /* already dead */ } }, graceMs)`,
with the escalation timer cleared on the child's `exit` event. Default `graceMs` to 8000. Wrap the
initial `SIGTERM` in try/catch too and swallow an `ESRCH` — a child that raced to exit is the normal
case, not an error. Do not build a recursive descendant-PID walker: the process-group mechanism handles
arbitrarily deep descendant trees with one syscall per signal and has no TOCTOU race.

Add the wall-clock timer: `setTimeout(() =&gt; { killTree(child.pid); recordEvent(db, task.id, { type: 'TIMEOUT' }, 'system'); }, wallClockCapMs)`,
cleared with `clearTimeout` on the child's `exit` event so a completed session cannot record a late
`TIMEOUT`. Note explicitly for the executor: RESEARCH.md Pitfall 5 warns that
`--permission-mode acceptEdits` is NOT a "no prompts, ever" guarantee — headless hangs remain possible
because the permission engine still gates non-edit tool categories. The wall-clock cap is the real
backstop for that class, not the permission-mode choice, so it must never be optional or disable-able.

Add an exported `resolveCaps(input)` returning `{ maxTurns, wallClockCapMs, setupTimeoutMs }` with D-11's
resolution order — task row value, then `.fleet.yml`, then Fleet config, then the built-in defaults
`40` turns and `1_800_000` ms. `tasks.max_turns` and `tasks.wall_clock_cap_ms` are nullable, so `null`
means inherit; do not treat `0` as inherit, reject it. Validate each resolved value as a positive integer
and throw a typed error naming the offending source when it is not, rather than coercing.

Extend `src/runner/worktree-runner.test.ts` for every `<behavior>` case, driving the real fixture rather
than mocking `child_process`. Use `process.kill(pid, 0)` as the existence probe and assert on the thrown
error's `code`, never on its message text. For the SIGTERM-ignoring case add a fixture scenario or reuse
`hang` with a trap; RESEARCH.md Assumption A2 flags that only the SIGTERM path was verified live, so this
is the test that converts A2 from an assumption into an observed fact on this machine. Set an explicit
per-test timeout of 15 seconds on the kill tests so a slow box does not flake.
  </action>
  <verify>

  </verify>

  <action>
Harden the stdout handling in `src/runner/worktree-runner.ts`.

**Defensive parsing (D-14).** Use `node:readline`'s `createInterface({ input: child.stdout })` so partial
lines are assembled correctly, and import `parseLine` from `src/runner/rate-limit.ts` (relocated in Task
3) rather than writing a second defensive parser. One parse attempt per line inside try/catch; a `null`
result is skipped silently. An unknown `type` value is a forward-compatible no-op and is never thrown
on — SPIKE-04 already caught a live `rate_limit_event` line that no documented schema table lists, and
CLAUDE.md §A2 instructs exactly this tolerance.

**The `apiKeySource` assertion (D-02, BILL-07).** On the FIRST line that parses as
`type === 'system' && subtype === 'init'`, read its `apiKeySource` field. When the value is anything
other than the string `none`, immediately `killTree(child.pid)` and
`recordEvent(db, task.id, { type: 'CRASH', reason: 'apiKeySource=' + observed }, 'system')`, then stop
processing the stream. This must happen before a single turn is billed. This assertion is the ONE
guarantee that holds regardless of which path tried to inject a credential — an environment variable, an
`apiKeyHelper` in any settings file, or a route not yet imagined — because it is observational rather
than static. RESEARCH.md Pitfall 1 documents a real case (`anthropics/claude-code#39903`) where a
subagent re-acquires a credential the top-level spawn env excluded; env allowlisting alone cannot close
that, and this check is the backstop for it. Treat an absent `apiKeySource` field the same as a wrong
value — a schema change that removes it must fail loudly, never silently pass.

**Session id capture (D-16, RUN-06).** Persist `session_id` opportunistically from the FIRST parsed line
that carries it, whatever its `type` — SPIKE-04 observed it on `system/init`, `assistant`,
`rate_limit_event`, and `result`, so it is available early and often. Write it through the task service,
never with a direct `db.update`. Add a `resume` path to `buildSpawnArgv` that, when a stored session id
is supplied, appends `--resume <id>` and `--fork-session` and reuses the same worktree `cwd`, so the
resumed run gets a fresh session id while the original transcript stays intact for audit.

**Observability only (RUN-05).** stdout is best-effort observability and is NEVER the state-transition
source. Broadcast every parsed line to the in-process event bus, but persist only the lifecycle-
significant ones to `events`, and let the process-exit path decide the terminal transition. A
`HOOK_STOP`-shaped object appearing on stdout must NOT be forwarded into `recordEvent` — hooks own that
transition and they arrive in Phase 3. Writing `tasks.status` from two places is the named anti-pattern
in ARCHITECTURE.md and this is the exact place it would creep in. Do NOT adopt `--include-hook-events`:
SPIKE-04 surfaced it as undocumented-but-present and D-15 defers it to Phase 3 precisely so a second
transition source is not created now.

Extend `src/runner/worktree-runner.test.ts` for every `<behavior>` case, driving the real fixture
scenarios. For the "no second transition source" assertion, feed a `HOOK_STOP`-shaped line through the
handler and assert the `events` table gained no `HOOK_STOP` row.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>npm test -- src/runner/worktree-runner.test.ts</automated>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>
    - `npm test -- src/runner/worktree-runner.test.ts` exits 0 with a test for each `<behavior>` case.
    - A test runs the `malformed-line` scenario and asserts the run reaches a terminal `result` and the task is not `failed` on account of the bad lines.
    - A test runs the `unknown-event` scenario and asserts zero `events` rows were created for the two unknown types.
    - A test runs the `api-key-source-leak` scenario and asserts a `CRASH` event row exists whose payload string contains the observed value, that `tasks.status` is `failed`, and that no `assistant`-derived observation was recorded.
    - A test asserts a `system/init` line with the `apiKeySource` field entirely absent also triggers the kill-and-`CRASH` path.
    - A test asserts `tasks.session_id` is a non-empty string after the `happy-path` run.
    - A test asserts a resume argv contains `--resume` followed by the stored id and also contains `--fork-session`.
    - A test feeds a `HOOK_STOP`-shaped stdout line and asserts no `HOOK_STOP` row appears in `events`.
    - `grep -rn "include-hook-events" src/runner/` returns no matches.
    - `npm test` (whole `unit` project) exits 0.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>No stdout line can crash the daemon, drive a state transition, or let a session with a non-subscription credential source bill a single turn.</done>
